deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no derivations. It is a list headed 'Doktorthemata', i.e. proposed dissertation topics. The previous page has Staatsexamen topics and the next page continues the list with more number-theory topics. The entries are as follows.

(1) A critical comparison of the various proofs of the finiteness of the invariants of binary forms. The proofs named are by Gordan, by Jordan (with a footnote *), by Mertens, and 'two by me'. The two Hilbert proofs are presumably his 1888 Göttinger Nachrichten / Math. Ann. 33 proof and his 1890 Math. Ann. 36 Basissatz proof. The topic also covers combining the proofs, an upper bound for the number of invariants (in Jordan's sense: bounds on degrees and number of generators), and Sylvester's counting calculus (Cayley–Sylvester enumeration of seminvariants). The footnote *) reads 'Liouville's Journal (3) V S. 345 und mehrere Noten in den Comptes rendus'. This is Jordan, 'Sur les covariants des formes binaires', J. math. pures appl. (3) 5 (1879), 345 ff., and Jordan's CR notes, which give explicit degree bounds.

(2) Find the theorems in the ternary domain that correspond to 'my theorem on the symbol [ ] = 1 + ΔD + ... = 1 − DΔ ...' and its use for completing invariants ('die Ergänzung von Invarianten durch ...'). The reference is Hilbert's 1887 Math. Ann. 28 paper on the binary domain. There D and Δ are the two Cayley–Aronhold differential operators on the coefficients (the raising and lowering operators of sl2). [ ] is an operator series, a polynomial in DΔ with rational coefficients. It projects an arbitrary function of the coefficients onto the kernel of one operator, i.e. it completes a 'source' to an invariant or covariant. The two expansions are of the form [ ] = 1 + c1 ΔD + c2 Δ²D² + ... and the dual form 1 − c1' DΔ + .... The task is to find the sl3 analogue. The exact coefficients are not written on the page.

(3) Crossed out: give a purely algebraic proof, by elimination theory, of a Kronecker theorem about a 'possibility' (word illegible) when the functional determinant ≠ 0.

(4) Study arithmetically the forms admitting linear transformations into themselves: the tetrahedral, octahedral and icosahedral forms, citing Klein, Ikosaeder p. 51 ff. That is, carry out the decomposition of the integers of the number fields defined by the associated irrationalities into prime ideals.

(5) Actually write down the finite groups of linear substitutions in 4 and 5 variables, taking the literature into account, following the general principles of C. Jordan and H. Minkowski.

(6) Generalize Gauss's theory of mechanical quadrature to the approximation of functions by functions of algebraic fields (algebraic function fields), with a cross-reference to 'schwarzes Heft II, die ersten Blätter'.

(7) Prove Fermat's theorem that x^l + y^l + z^l = 0 is impossible, in the case where l does not divide (the numerators of) the first (l−3)/2 Bernoulli numbers. This is Kummer's regularity condition. The proof is to avoid ideal theory and use only the theory of higher congruences.

At the bottom: 'Fortsetzung auf dem Deckel' (continued on the cover).
errors: No mathematical errors. The statements are topic descriptions. The Fermat item correctly states Kummer's criterion: l divides none of the numerators of B_2, B_4, ..., B_{l-3}, i.e. the first (l−3)/2 nonzero even-index Bernoulli numbers.

results.what: Finiteness of binary invariants: comparison of the Gordan, Jordan, Mertens and Hilbert proofs, plus bounds on the number of generators.
results.modern_name: Gordan's finiteness theorem / Hilbert basis theorem; degree bounds for generators (Jordan bounds)

results.what: Projection operator [ ] built from D and Δ (power series in DΔ) mapping forms onto invariants; proposed generalization to ternary forms.
results.modern_name: sl2 projection onto highest-weight vectors (extremal projector); its sl3 analogue
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert 1887 (binary case); general extremal projectors due to Asherova–Smirnov–Tolstoy (1970s)

results.what: Arithmetic of number fields generated by the polyhedral (Klein) irrationalities.
results.modern_name: Arithmetic of icosahedral/octahedral/tetrahedral fields (A5, S4, A4 extensions)

results.what: Classification of finite linear groups in 4 and 5 variables using the Jordan and Minkowski principles.
results.modern_name: Classification of finite subgroups of GL4, GL5

results.what: Generalizing Gaussian quadrature to approximation by functions of algebraic function fields.
results.modern_name: Gaussian quadrature / orthogonal polynomial approximation on algebraic curves

results.what: Fermat's Last Theorem for regular primes, to be proved without ideal theory using higher congruences.
results.modern_name: Kummer's theorem for regular primes (Kummer's criterion)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a list of thesis proposals, not results. It documents Hilbert's research agenda c. 1890. The suggestion to extend his D/Δ projector to the ternary case is mildly interesting. Otherwise everything is standard for the period.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import bernoulli, fraction; fraction(bernoulli(32))[0] % 37 == 0
checkable.asserts: 37 divides the numerator of B_32 (index 32 ≤ 34 = l−3), so 37 fails the condition and is irregular.
31 is regular: it divides none of the first (31−3)/2 = 14 even-index Bernoulli numerators, so the stated case of Fermat applies.
Klein's icosahedral syzygy T^2 = -H^5 + 1728 f^5 among the invariant forms of Klein Ikosaeder (topic 4).

transcription_corrections: Line 3 begins 'Mertens und zwei von mir', not 'Gordan[?] und zwei von mir'; Mertens gave a proof of finiteness in 1886.
The names in line 2 are probably 'Beweise von Gordan, Jordan*)' (Jordan inserted with the footnote mark), not 'Jordan, Jordan'.

The footnote '*) Liouville's Journal (3) V S. 345 und mehrere Noten in den Comptes rendus' belongs to Jordan in the first item (Jordan, J. math. pures appl. (3) 5, 1879, p. 345), not to the Fermat item. The trailing 'Vgl.[?] *)' on the Fermat line is uncertain.
'Comptes rendus' is written as 'Comptes' with 'rendus' added beneath the line.
